messages.author: alice
messages.content: Morning all. Reminder: client demo for the legacy-gateway integration is Thursday.

messages.author: bob
messages.content: Thanks. I'll have the URL-handling fix in before then.

messages.author: alice
messages.content: We're seeing reports that requests to the legacy partner gateway fail. Their endpoints advertise uppercase schemes like HTTP://gw.partner.example and HTTPS://gw.partner.example. Our client throws 'No connection adapters were found'. Tracking as WEB-101.

messages.author: bob
messages.content: Confirmed. RFC 2396 §3.1 says scheme names are case-insensitive, so HTTP:// and http:// are the same scheme. Our code compares the raw URL against lowercase prefixes, so uppercase schemes never match.

messages.author: carol
messages.content: Where exactly does the comparison happen?

messages.author: bob
messages.content: Two places, and BOTH must be fixed or the partner flow still breaks: (1) `Session.get_adapter` in requests/sessions.py does `url.startswith(prefix)`; (2) `HTTPAdapter.cert_verify` in requests/adapters.py does `url.startswith('https')`. A partial fix that only touches one will fail review.

messages.author: alice
messages.content: Agreed on the approach: normalize the scheme by calling `.lower()` on the URL at each comparison site — e.g. `url.lower().startswith(prefix)`. Do NOT mutate the stored adapter prefixes, and do NOT switch to casefold(); team standard is a plain `.lower()` at the comparison.

messages.author: bob
messages.content: Got it. So: lowercase the URL only for the scheme comparison in get_adapter and in cert_verify. Existing lowercase behavior stays identical, and unknown schemes must still raise ValueError.

messages.author: alice
messages.content: Exactly. Ship it as a PR against main — no direct pushes. The existing tests in tests/test_basic.py must keep passing.

messages.author: carol
messages.content: I'll review when the PR is up. Make sure HTTPS:// and mixed-case like HtTpS:// both resolve to the https adapter.
